tasks.short: Seek third-party verification of the design.

steps.what: List energy design items already evidenced in the file.
Secure third-party verification of the building design.
Send only the evidence pack the verifier asked for.

tasks.design: Items in the energy-design list that already have a document in {DOCS} are marked, and the gaps are shown. The construction manager secures third-party verification, including for a Leadership in Energy Efficient Design submission where the project uses that scheme, and sends only the pack the verifier asked for. The list does not award a rating. A claim with no document is not sent.
tasks.previous_blocker: Evidence was assembled in a rush from inboxes, and a rating claim was made for a document nobody could find.
tasks.enabler_now: A credit item can be matched to a document id. The verifier's decision, and the relationship with them, stay human.
tasks.still_hard: A scheme whose evidence rules change, a design that almost complies, and a verifier who wants a test the project has not run.
tasks.human_edge: The manager knows which claim would be a stretch, and will not send it.
tasks.altitude: Gaps in the evidence file are visible. The manager still deals with the verifier and still decides what is sent. No rating is produced here.

reach.task: Assemble evidence for a third party and do not grade it yourself.
reach.learn: A matched document is not a rating. This manager still deals with the verifier.

evidence.claim: A file can show which named evidence items have a document id. It cannot award a building rating.

Sending evidence to a third party is the manager's act. A drafted claim must cite a document the file holds. The job digest's warning about reports that cite what they do not hold applies. The rating, if any, is the verifier's.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: A construction manager at a European contractor or client team. National building rules apply. A register does not replace a site visit.

Fields: Credit or evidence item id, and document id, produced by the project file. An item with no document id is a gap and is not described as met. If a required field is missing, the step stops and the manager finishes it by hand.
Native check: Match items in the existing document store before a new rating tool.
Any edit after approval voids the version and returns the item to the manager.
unknowns: Which verification scheme this project actually uses.
Who may correspond with the verifier.
research_questions: Are evidence items listed with document ids today?
Who pays the verifier and under which contract?

already_counted.description: The manager still deals with the verifier.
The manager still approves the pack.

incremental.description: The manager updates an evidence item when the scheme changes its rule.

approvals.approved_version: item ids and the document ids about to be sent

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Dealing with the verifier stays with the manager. Saving is the gap list, and it shrinks when evidence was never given a document id and the manager still hunts the file.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Train the crew on responsible building topics.

steps.what: Implement training on environmentally responsible building.
Record attendance without scoring employee skills.

tasks.design: Topics already written for environmentally responsible building are listed from {DOCS}. The construction manager implements the training with the crew on site and updates their practical knowledge in the room. Attendance can be recorded in the {LMS}. Skills are not scored. The list does not train anyone.
tasks.previous_blocker: Training was a toolbox talk from memory, and nobody could say later who had heard it.
tasks.enabler_now: A topic list can be opened. The session with the crew cannot be replaced by the list.
tasks.still_hard: A crew that changes every week, a language gap, and a topic that only matters if someone demonstrates it.
tasks.human_edge: The manager can see that the room has not understood, and can show the action rather than repeat the slide.
tasks.altitude: The topics are written down. The training stays with the manager and the crew. Attendance is not a judgement of a person.

reach.task: Run a session and record who attended, without grading character.
reach.learn: A topic list is not the session. This manager still teaches the crew.

evidence.claim: A catalogue can list topics. It cannot update a crew's practice on site.

The job digest says scoring staff on traits is high-risk and staff data in a roster or a monitor needs works-council consent. This task records attendance only if the existing learning record already allows it, and it stores no score.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: A construction manager at a European contractor or client team. National building rules apply. A register does not replace a site visit.

Fields: Topic id and title, produced by the catalogue. Attendance, if recorded, is a name and a date already kept by the learning record. No skill score field is added. If a required field is missing, the step stops and the manager finishes it by hand.
Native check: Use the existing topic notes and the existing learning record.
unknowns: Whether attendance may be recorded under the current works-council agreement.
Which topics are mandatory on this project.
research_questions: Does the learning record already store site attendance?

already_counted.description: The manager still runs the training.
The manager still records attendance without a score.

incremental.description: The manager adds a topic when a new site rule needs a talk.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The session is the task. Saving is finding the topic note, and it is small. If attendance may not be stored, that recording step stays a paper the manager already keeps.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Compare green and ordinary construction costs.

steps.what: Sum short-term and long-term costs for both options.
Compare environmental impacts the costs do not show.
Sign the construction budget that uses one option.

tasks.design: Short-term and long-term costs for the green option and the ordinary option are summed in {ERP} on the same rates. The construction manager compares environmental impacts the costs do not show and signs the budget that adopts one option. The sum does not choose. An option with a missing long-term cost is marked incomplete and is not treated as cheaper.
tasks.previous_blocker: Green was argued as a feeling, or ordinary was chosen because only the build cost had been added up.
tasks.enabler_now: Two options with quantities and rates can be summed the same way. The impact and the choice stay with the manager.
tasks.still_hard: A long-term cost nobody has a rate for, and an impact that is real but not in money.
tasks.human_edge: The manager can say the cheaper build creates a cost the client will pay later, or the reverse.

ambition.what: Compare green and ordinary cost for a small package in the same week, not only for the flagship building.

tasks.altitude: The two sums exist before the argument. The manager still weighs the impact and still signs the budget.

reach.task: Put two options on the same cost basis before preferring the lower-impact one.
reach.learn: Equal sums are not the decision. This manager still signs the budget.

evidence.claim: Quantities and rates can sum two options, including a later-year cost if a rate exists. A missing rate cannot be shown as zero.
Adopting a budget is the manager's decision. The job digest says budget figures come from the finance records and a person checks the story against them. No vendor saving percentage is used.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: A construction manager at a European contractor or client team. National building rules apply. A register does not replace a site visit.

Fields: Option id, cost code, year, quantity, and rate, produced by the two takeoffs and the rate library. A blank long-term rate keeps the option incomplete. If a required field is missing, the step stops and the manager finishes it by hand.
Native check: Use the existing cost codes for both options.
Any edit after approval voids the version and returns the item to the manager.
unknowns: Which long-term costs the client wants in the comparison.
Who signs the budget if it exceeds the manager's limit.
research_questions: Do green and ordinary options share cost codes?
Which long-term costs have no rate?

already_counted.description: The manager still compares impacts the costs omit.
The manager still signs the budget.

incremental.description: The manager adds a long-term rate when one becomes available.

approvals.approved_version: option ids and the cost comparison shown to the manager

time_saved_range_pct.basis: If long-term rates are missing, the manager still builds the comparison by hand and the saving stays near the low end. Complete rates keep the high end, and the impact judgement remains.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Apply green building strategies on the project.

steps.what: Show energy and carbon figures already on the project.
Apply green building strategies on this project.
Record which strategy was chosen and why.

tasks.design: Energy and carbon figures already calculated for the project are shown from {ERP}. The construction manager applies the green building strategy on the project, to reduce energy cost or other harm, and records what was chosen. The figures do not apply the strategy. A measure with no figure is not treated as a saving.
tasks.previous_blocker: A strategy was named in the bid and then quietly dropped when the programme got tight.
tasks.enabler_now: A figure that exists can be shown. Applying the strategy on a live site is still the manager's work.
tasks.still_hard: A trade who bids the ordinary detail, a programme that has no day left for the better detail, and a harm that is not in the figure.
tasks.human_edge: The manager can keep a strategy in the work when it would be easier to let it slip.
tasks.altitude: The figures are visible. Applying the strategy stays with the manager on the project. The sheet does not claim a saving the project has not built.

reach.task: Hold a stated measure through to the way the work is actually done.
reach.learn: A figure is not the measure. This manager still applies it on the project.

evidence.claim: Stored figures can be shown. They cannot install a detail or change a sequence on site.
Claiming an environmental result that was not built would be a false report. The manager records only what was chosen. No automated claim of carbon saved is sent out.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: A construction manager at a European contractor or client team. National building rules apply. A register does not replace a site visit.

Fields: Measure id and a figure, produced by a calculation already on the project. A measure with no figure is listed as not quantified. If a required field is missing, the step stops and the manager finishes it by hand.
Native check: Read the figures from the existing project cost and design notes.
unknowns: Which strategies the contract actually requires.
Who checks that a strategy survived into the built work.
research_questions: Are energy and carbon figures stored per measure?
Which bid strategies were dropped on the last project?

already_counted.description: The manager still applies the strategy on the project.
The manager still records the choice.

incremental.description: The manager attaches a figure when a measure is newly calculated.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Applying the strategy is site and design judgement and stays with the manager. Saving is showing figures that already exist, and it is small when those figures were never calculated.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The manager still deals with the third-party verifier, still trains the crew, and still chooses the green strategy. Cost comparisons of green and ordinary options can be calculated first.
reach: Chief sustainability officers compare whole-life cost with environmental impact, and the project choice stays with this manager.
Education administrators run a training session, and this job learns attendance is not a score of the person.
skills_to_grow: Send a verifier only evidence the project file actually holds.
Compare green and ordinary costs on the same codes before arguing for either.
role.ambitious_version: A small package gets a green and ordinary cost comparison in the same week, and the strategy on site is still the manager's.
